title: How Google's Antitrust Trial Could Change Internet Search
description: The Department of Justice filed a lawsuit against Google, claiming that the company violated of the Sherman Act.
lead: In the ongoing court battle between Google and the U.S. Justice Department over whether the company has violated an antitrust law, the stakes are high. The outcome of the 10-week trial, which will be decided by U.S. District Judge Amit Mehta, could fundamentally change the way people search the internet and reduce revenue for the company that has the most common search engine for online users.

title: Apple search payment is the heart of the antitrust case against Google, says judge
description: While the Department of Justice has accused Google of a range of anti-competitive behaviors, the judge in the case has...
lead: While the Department of Justice has accused Google of a range of anti-competitive behaviors, the judge in the case has said that the Apple search payment is “the heart” of the matter. The implication is clear. If that deal is illegal, then Google will lose the case, and the company may have to be broken up. Conversely, if the court finds that the payment was legal, then Google likely wins, as the other charges are comparatively minor …

title: Why Google, Bing And Other Search Engines’ Embrace Of Generative AI Threatens $68 Billion SEO Industry
description: Analysis from a Texas A&M associate professor of information and operations management.
lead: Google, Microsoft and others boast that generative artificial intelligence tools like ChatGPT will make searching the internet better than ever for users. For example, rather than having to wade through a sea of URLs, users will be able to just get an answer combed from the entire internet. There are also some concerns with the rise of AI-fueled search engines, such as the opacity over where information comes from, the potential for “hallucinated” answers and copyright issues.

title: Is Google Search better than the rest? And is that fair?
description: As the US takes the tech giant to court in a massive antitrust trial, allegations that Google makes itself worse to earn more in ad money continue.
lead: The US government’s potentially landmark antitrust trial against Google is around halfway through, and so far we’ve heard from the tech giant itself as well as Apple, Microsoft and others. What it all boils down to is that regulators think Google holds an unfair monopoly share of the search engine market, more than 80 per cent, which it maintains through deals with other companies to make Google Search the default. Google argues its product is simply preferred because it’s the best.

title: Google is actively looking to insert different types of ads in its generative AI search
description: Google is planning to experiment with different native ad formats for its generative AI based search experince.
lead: Google confirmed on its earnings call that it is working on different ad formats for its generative AI-powered search experience — Google shared some ideas earlier this year and the mention in the earnings call could indicate that a rollout could happen sooner rather than later. This project is particularly important for the company as the majority of Google’s revenue still comes from ads despite several attempts to diversify its revenue sources through Google Cloud, services and other bets including hardware.

title: Google brushes off ad controversies as search, YouTube regain momentum
description: More users are searching for deals ahead of the holidays, with the company angling to help marketers reach price-conscious consumers.
lead: The tech giant’s core search business and YouTube were bright spots. Search and Other, its largest segment, was up 11% YoY to $44.02 billion while YouTube climbed 12% YoY to $7.95 billion, supported by spending on both brand-building and direct response campaigns. Meanwhile, revenue from Google’s advertising network that helps brands place ads around the web declined 3% YoY to $7.67 billion. The positive results give the company momentum heading into the key holiday period and suggest Google has effectively brushed off a series of recent controversies related to its ads business.

title: Inside Google’s Plan to Stop Apple From Getting Serious About Search (Published 2023)
description: Google has worried for years that Apple would one day expand its internet search technology, and has been working on ways to prevent that from happening.
lead: For years, Google watched with increasing concern as Apple improved its search technology, not knowing whether its longtime partner and sometimes competitor would eventually build its own search engine. Those fears ratcheted up in 2021, when Google paid Apple around $18 billion to keep Google’s search engine the default selection on iPhones, according to two people with knowledge of the partnership, who were not authorized to discuss it publicly. The same year, Apple’s iPhone search tool, Spotlight, began showing users richer web results like those they could have found on Google.

title: Google paid a whopping $26.3 billion in 2021 to be the default search engine everywhere
description: Default search status doesn’t come cheap, but it’s worth it to Google.
lead: We knew Google paid handsomely to be the default browser in Safari, Firefox, and elsewhere. Now we know, after years of guessing, exactly what it cost. The US v. Google antitrust trial is about many things, but more than anything, it’s about the power of defaults. Even if it’s easy to switch browsers or platforms or search engines, the one that appears when you turn it on matters a lot. Google obviously agrees and has paid a staggering amount to make sure it is the default: testimony in the trial revealed that Google spent a total of $26.3 billion in 2021 to be the default search engine in multiple browsers, phones, and platforms.

lead: (Bloomberg) -- The former head of search at Alphabet Inc.'s Google told colleagues in February 2019 that his team was "getting too involved with ads for the good of the product and company," according to emails shown at the Justice Department's landmark antitrust trial against the search giant. Google maintains a firewall between its ads and search teams so that its engineers can innovate on Google's search engine, unsullied by the influence of the team whose goal is to maximize advertising revenue. But in February 2019, testimony at the antitrust trial revealed Tuesday, Google internally declared a "Code Yellow" amid concerns the company might not meet its goals for search revenue for the quarter.

title: Here’s a rare look at Google’s most lucrative search queries
description: iPhones, insurance, and streaming are where the search money is.
lead: Thanks to a newly public list, we get to see where Google’s ad money comes from, one search result at a time. Not all Google searches make Google money. Google often says that it only shows ads on about 20 percent of queries, the ones it calls “commercial queries.” You can probably guess what qualifies. “US president in 1836” is not something you type when you’re about to buy something; neither is “facebook” because all you’re looking for is Facebook. But if you type in “best new car 2023” or “cheap flights to London” there are a lot of advertisers that would like to be the first thing you see, and there’s a lot of money for Google to be made in the process.

title: New Google Trial Docs May Explain Why Search Sucks So Bad Now
description: New documents in the Google antitrust trial show how tension between product and advertising teams could lead to degraded experiences for consumers.
lead: New documents in the Google antitrust trial show how tension between product and advertising teams could lead to degraded experiences for consumers. The Department of Justice and Google just rumbled their way past the halfway point of a landmark antitrust trial vying to answer a potentially industry-rupturing question: Does Google maintain its ironfisted stranglehold over internet search results because of its superior innovation or as a byproduct of ruthless anti-competitive jockeying and closed-door dealings? New documents revealed during the historic monopoly trial over the past week seem to lend more weight to the latter argument, and they could help explain why Google’s once dazzling search results anecdotally feel like they are getting worse for some.

title: Why Google and Meta owe news publishers much more than you think – and billions more than they’d like to admit

lead: In a time of war and populism, the world needs quality information and credible news outlets. Local news is a part of this healthy ecology. But news publishers have struggled to find ways to make money in recent years – especially as referral traffic and ad revenue from social media sites continue to fall. The monopoly power of large platforms, and the control they exert over news distribution, was one reason Australia’s competition authorities introduced the News Media Bargaining Code in 2021.

title: What We Learn About the Behavioral Economics of Defaults From the Google Search Monopolization Case

lead: Paul Heidhues worked on topics in competition economics such as input-market bargaining power, merger control, collusion, and the functioning of markets when consumers are partly driven by psychological factors that the classical consumer model abstracts from. Paul is a member of DG Competition’s European Advisory Group on Competition Policy, of the UK‘s Competition and Markets Authority’s Academic Panel, and of the Bundeskartellamt’s Arbeitskreis Kartellrecht. title: Google Search Is an Illegal Monopoly, US Judge Rules

Alphabet Announces Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2025 Results (PDF file) https://s206.q4cdn.com/479360582/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/2025q4-alphabet-earnings-release.pdf Alphabet 2025 Q4 Earnings Call - YouTube Google's annual revenue tops $400 billion for the first time | The Verge https://www.theverge.com/news/874161/google-400-billion-revenue-q4-2025-earnings Alphabet's consolidated revenue for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025 increased 18% year-over-year to $113,828 million (approximately ¥17.8 trillion) due to accelerated growth in Google Services and Google Cloud. Operating income for the same period increased 16% year-over-year to $35,934 million (approximately ¥5.61 trillion), and net income increased 30% year-over-year to $34,455 million (approximately ¥5.37 trillion). For the full fiscal year 2025, Alphabet's annual sales exceeded the $400 billion mark for the first time, reaching $402.836 billion (approximately ¥62.8 trillion), up 15% from the previous year. Full-year operating profit was $129.039 billion (approximately ¥20.1 trillion), up 15% from the previous year, and net profit was $132.17 billion (approximately ¥20.6 trillion), up 32% from the previous year. Fourth-quarter revenue for Google Services increased 14% year-over-year to $95.862 billion (approximately 15 trillion yen), driven by strong performance from Google Search and YouTube. Operating profit for the division was $40.132 billion (approximately 6.26 trillion yen), up 22% from $32.836 billion in the same period last year. Revenue breakdown: Google Search and Other increased 17%, YouTube Advertising increased 9%, and Subscriptions, Platforms & Devices increased 17%. YouTube's combined annual advertising and subscription revenue is expected to exceed $60 billion for the first time in 2025. Additionally, the number of paid subscriptions for all consumer services has reached 325 million, with Gemini Enterprise paying seats exceeding 8 million in the four months since its launch, and Gemini's monthly active users exceeding 750 million. Google Cloud revenue grew significantly, increasing 48% year-over-year to $17.664 billion (approximately JPY 2.76 trillion), driven by strong demand for AI infrastructure and solutions. The division's operating profit increased 154% to $5.313 billion (approximately JPY 829 billion), up from $2.093 billion in the same period last year. The company's AI investments are contributing to its profits, with its cloud business's annual revenue run rate exceeding $70 billion by the end of 2025. Fourth-quarter revenue for the Other Bets segment, which primarily includes revenue from autonomous driving services, was $370 million (approximately ¥57.7 billion), down from $400 million in the same period last year. The segment's operating loss widened to $3.617 billion (approximately ¥564 billion), up from $1.174 billion (approximately ¥184 billion) in the same period last year. Operating expenses for the same period included $2.1 billion (approximately ¥328 billion) in employee compensation expenses related to Waymo, the autonomous driving division, which was the primary factor behind the wider loss. Sundar Pichai, chairman and CEO of Google, said, 'Following the launch of Gemini 3, usage intensity per user has increased, and our AI investments and infrastructure are driving overall business growth.' He also predicted that the company will spend $175 billion to $185 billion in capital expenditures in 2026 to meet demand. Pichai also stated that the company is pursuing a full-stack approach to AI, expanding its options for computing resources with both GPUs and its own TPUs, while also mentioning strengthening its data center and energy infrastructure. As an example of efficiency improvements, he mentioned that Gemini's cost per serving will be reduced by 78% by 2025. On the model side, he explained that Gemini 3 Pro is at the core of inference and multimodal understanding, and that adoption is progressing at the fastest pace. On the product side, the integration of Gemini 3 into the search 'AI Mode' and 'AI Overview' has led to increased usage due to deeper understanding and interactive experiences. Furthermore, CEO Pichai emphasized that Google is simultaneously expanding in multiple areas, including the introduction of the ' Universal Commerce Protocol ,' a common standard for connecting AI agents with retail and payment systems, Project Genie , which creates a generative world, and the restructuring of Chrome with AI capabilities in mind .

title: Following an EU decision allowing those harmed by Google's advertising market monopoly to seek damages, more than 20 news publishers are demanding over 100 billion yen in compensation from Google.
description: In September 2025, the European Commission, the EU's policy-making body, fined Google €2.95 billion (approximately ¥500 billion) for violating antitrust laws by distorting competition in the ad tech industry. The European Commission indicated that individuals or companies affected by the anti-competitive practices revealed in this case could seek damages, leading several publishing groups to file lawsuits seeking a total of more than €640 million (approximately ¥118 billion). European publishers seek £552m+ from Google claiming ad market abuse - Press Gazette https://pressgazette.co.uk/marketing/european-publishers-seek-552m-from-google-claiming-ad-market-abuse/ Google sells ads on its websites and applications, acting as an intermediary between advertisers who want to place ads online and publishers (third-party websites and apps) who can provide ad space. Advertisers and publishers utilize digital tools from the ad tech industry to display real-time ads that are not linked to search queries, and Google offers several ad tech services that act as intermediaries between advertisers and publishers for ad placement on websites and mobile apps. In June 2023, the European Commission warned Google that it was distorting competition in the ad tech industry and violating antitrust laws. In response, Google proposed selling its ad tech business, but the proposal was rejected. Then, on September 5, 2025, local time, the European Commission stated that 'its own investigation has shown that Google holds a dominant position in the publisher ad server market with DFP, and in the open web programmatic ad buying tools market with Google Ads and DV360. Both markets cover the entire European Economic Area (EEA),' and announced that it would impose a fine of 2.95 billion euros (approximately 500 billion yen) on Google for violating antitrust laws in the ad tech market. Google fined over 500 billion yen by the EU for violating antitrust laws - GIGAZINE In its announcement that it would fine Google, the European Commission stated that 'any individual or company affected by anti-competitive conduct as described in this case may file a lawsuit in the courts of a Member State to seek damages. Even if the European Commission fines Google, national courts may order damages without deducting the European Commission's fine.' This means that damages suffered by individual companies will be considered separately from the fine imposed on Google by the European Commission. Therefore, more than 20 publishers from the Czech Republic, Estonia, France, Hungary, Finland, the Netherlands, Poland, and Sweden have jointly filed a lawsuit against Google seeking a total of 640 million euros (approximately 118 billion yen). In the lawsuit, they argue that 'if Google had not created a less competitive market, advertising revenue would have been much higher, and the cost of advertising technology services would have been much lower.' This lawsuit is being funded by Prague-based litigation financing firm LitFin, which has an agreement to cover the costs if they lose and receive a share of the compensation if they win. Matej Pardo, Chief Operating Officer of LitFin, said, 'The European Commission's final decision has determined that Google's abuse of its position across the entire advertising technology stack was illegal. Now is the time for publishers who have suffered damages as a result to receive compensation. By filing a class-action lawsuit, we can leverage economies of scale and enable small businesses across Europe to file similar lawsuits. Otherwise, it would be difficult to sue a financially powerful opponent like Google.' The U.S. Department of Justice has also ruled on Google's illegal monopoly in its advertising business, and in May 2025, a proposal was submitted to break up Google's major advertising-related businesses, arguing that Google had illegally acquired and maintained a monopolistic position in the advertising technology market. The Department of Justice has stated that Google should sell its advertising businesses, AdX and DFP, but Google is strongly protesting, calling it impossible - GIGAZINE In response, an American publisher filed a lawsuit against Google in January 2026, claiming that 'Google's advertising technology is deceptive and manipulative.' Google countered the allegations of monopoly by stating, 'These claims are unfounded. Advertisers and publishers have many options, and they choose Google's advertising technology tools because they are effective, affordable, and easy to use.' A ruling regarding Google's advertising technology monopoly is likely to be made sometime in 2026.

title: Google AI Overviews: 97% of Citations From Top 20 [2026]

lead: Google’s AI Overviews have quietly rewritten the rules of search visibility, and a new dataset from Semrush spells out exactly what it now takes to get cited. That is not a minor tweak to search behavior. It is a structural filter that decides which sites get seen by an AI summary and which ones simply disappear from view, even if they rank respectably on page one.

title: AI Mode vs ChatGPT vs Perplexity: 38x Traffic Gap [2026]
description: Google AI Mode, ChatGPT, and Perplexity compared as Google Search replacements: pricing, traffic share, EU rules, and which one Ireland should actually use.
lead: Type a question into Google on a laptop in Dublin today and there’s a decent chance the first thing you see isn’t a list of blue links. Google opened AI Mode to all US users on May 20, 2025, and by its I/O 2026 developer event in May it announced the feature had crossed 1 billion monthly users worldwide, a figure Google repeated in July 2026 while stressing AI Mode still requires no subscription, and Ireland is part of that rollout. title: Can Websites Skip Google's AI Summaries? EU Regulators Seek Publisher Feedback
description: EU antitrust regulators gather publisher feedback on Google's plan to let websites opt out of AI search features without losing search rank.
lead: European Union antitrust regulators issued a questionnaire to web publishers to evaluate Google’s new opt-out mechanism for AI Search. European competition authorities are actively gathering feedback from digital publishers to determine whether Google‘s proposed AI search controls offer fair protection for web creators. According to a questionnaire reviewed by Reuters, regulators want to know if website owners feel confident opting out of AI-generated search features without seeing their traditional search visibility drop.

title: How AI slop is turning Google search into a gatekeeper that harms Milwaukee businesses and civic life
description: Argues that Google's Gemini-powered AI summaries turn search from a directory into a gatekeeper, creating a 'zero-click' economy in which Google keeps attention and traffic while publishers, local businesses and independent experts lose their audiences.
lead: For much of the internet’s history, search engines functioned as directories. Users entered a question, received a list of links, and decided for themselves which sources deserved attention. Google did not create that model, but it became such a dominant force in the early 2000s that “Google” entered the English language as a verb synonymous with online search. But in March of 2024, the search engine suddenly replaced the fundamental way people search for and consume information.

title: How Many Searches on Google Per Day in 2026? (New Data)
description: Google continues to dominate with more than 16.4 billion searches daily. Find detailed Google search statistics inside to know more.
lead: Google remains the world’s most popular search engine, processing an estimated 16.4 billion searches per day. With over 5.06 billion users globally, Google dominates the search engine market with a 91.1% share, making it the go-to platform for finding information online. Back in 1999, it processed just 1 billion searches per year. By 2016, that number had surged past 2 trillion annually. Now, Google handles around 5.9 trillion searches per year, reflecting its deep integration into everyday life.

title: Google's AI answer engine is quietly strangling open web
description: Google’s AI-driven search is starving publishers of traffic, threatening the open web and forcing regulators to act
lead: On Aug. 20, Google unveiled a small, almost bureaucratic-sounding feature: a "Preferred Sources" button that publishers can embed on their own websites so readers can flag them as a favourite source across Search, Discover and Google News. Framed as a gesture of goodwill toward an embattled news industry, the announcement was in fact something closer to an admission. When the world's dominant gatekeeper of information starts building buttons to nudge a fraction of lost traffic back toward the websites it increasingly bypasses, it is because the underlying architecture of the web's economy has already broken.

title: AI Platforms Gain Ground Without Denting Google Search Traffic, BofA Says
description: Google’s web traffic held steady in August even as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and other artificial intelligence platforms continued to attract... Read More
lead: Google’s web traffic held steady in August even as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and other artificial intelligence platforms continued to attract users, according to a Bank of America analysis of Similarweb data. The figures suggest generative AI is expanding the broader market for online search and information rather than significantly displacing Google. Global daily visits to Google increased 3% from a year earlier to 2.8 billion. ChatGPT recorded 181 million daily web visits, down 5% year over year but up 4% from July.

description: MOUNTAIN VIEW, CA – Google is changing the way AdSense counts display advertising impressions, a move the company says will bring its measurement methodology in line with industry standards but could result in publishers reporting fewer impressions. lead: MOUNTAIN VIEW, CA – Google is changing the way AdSense counts display advertising impressions, a move the company says will bring its measurement methodology in line with industry standards but could result in publishers reporting fewer impressions. Beginning February 17, 2027, Google AdSense and Google Ad Manager will move display advertising from a “count-on-download” methodology to what Google calls “begin-to-render.”

title: Google rolls out pay-per-value AI licensing program to publishers
description: Google has been quietly scaling a pay-per-value AI licensing scheme for publishers. Though some critics are skeptical of its
lead: Google has been quietly scaling a pay-per-value AI licensing scheme for publishers. But critics say the program looks less like a meaningful payout and more like a legal fig leaf. The tech giant, which has steered clear of the large lump-sum licensing deals struck between other AI rivals like OpenAI and major news publishers, has been quietly testing a Search Console-based program that pays publishers when their content “significantly” contributes to AI-generated responses across Gemini, AI Overviews and AI mode, according to multiple industry sources close to the situation.

title: Google Is Hurting Gaming Websites, and Journalists Are Paying the Price
description: Google holds roughly 91% of search, and AI Overviews are cutting clicks to publishers. Here's what that means for gaming websites and the people working at them
lead: I’m beyond tired of talking about layoffs in gaming journalism. I’m tired of seeing talented people lose their jobs, and I’m even more tired of watching strangers celebrate it without understanding what is actually happening. The latest round of cuts at IGN dragged all of that frustration back to the surface, but this is a conversation I’ve wanted to have for a long time now. Honestly, it’s long overdue.

title: Daily Mirror Owner Reach Plans 220 Editorial Cuts as Google Traffic Retreats

lead: Reach plc plans to remove about 220 editorial roles while creating roughly 60 new ones, a net reduction of about 160 jobs at the owner of the Daily Mirror, Daily Express and scores of regional news sites. The proposal puts a number on the publisher’s response to falling search traffic: fewer roles devoted to volume, more investment in subscriptions and long-form video.

title: ‘I miss old Google’: readers tell us how they search the internet in the age of AI
description: A feature called AI Overviews has been a profound change, and the browsing habits of billions of people are shifting
lead: Google has put artificial intelligence at the front and center of its search bar. The most-visited site on the internet still shows the same list of links to users, but they have to scroll past a summarized response from an AI chatbot, a feature Google calls AI Overviews. The change to what was once the gateway to the rest of the internet has been profound, and the browsing habits of billions of people are shifting.

title: Google turns 28: Searching for answers in a world it helped create
description: From a $220,000 search business to a $400-billion-plus technology empire, Google has spent nearly three decades shaping the internet and its advertising economy. Now, as AI transforms discovery, the company must navigate an ecosystem it helped create
lead: Google celebrates its 28th birthday, reflecting on its evolution from a search engine to a major player in digital advertising and content distribution, particularly through its acquisition of YouTube in 2006. The company has seen significant revenue growth, with advertising accounting for a large portion of its income, but faces increasing competition from other platforms like Meta and regulatory scrutiny regarding its market dominance.

title: Google Is Paying About 100 Digital Publishers for AI Overviews

title: WashU research finds gaps in Google AI Overview citations, claims
description: With the advent of Google AI Overviews, Google has unprecedented editorial control over what users read and know, according to Jacob Montgomery, a political scientist in Arts & Sciences at Washington University in St. Louis.
lead: In the broadest independent audit to date, researchers found AI Overviews appeared in 13.7% of searches. Google generally cites credible sources, but citations don’t guarantee accuracy: about 11% of verifiable claims lacked support or contradicted cited sources. Since its launch in 1998, Google, the world’s leading search engine, has transformed how people find information online. For years, search results appeared as ranked lists of sources: Google decided what to show, but users decided what to read and whom to trust.

title: Google’s early attempt to pay websites for AI answers is struggling

lead: Google’s shift to AI-powered search has upended the way the world’s largest search engine generates web traffic, rankling large and small publishers alike. In recent months, the company has experimented with paying publishers when their content appears in AI answers, but a new report claims the payouts in this pilot program are miniscule. That has publishers in the program, as well as those watching from the sidelines, feeling skeptical.

title: Google: Unequal AI Payments to Publishers
description: Google compensates around 100 publishers for the use of their content in AI Previews, AI Mode, and Gemini.
lead: 💡Why it matters — Regulatory and legal pressure could challenge Google's current compensation model for content used by its AIs. Google's program that compensates publishers for the use of their articles in its AI responses involves disparate amounts, ranging from less than $1,000 to over a million per year. This volatility comes as the European Union investigates, a ruling in Germany redefines the nature of AI Snippets, and complaints pile up regarding declining traffic.

title: Google AI contribution pilot earns publishers one-tenth of 1% of ad revenues
description: Reports say the roughly 100 publishers in Google's pilot that pays for content contributing to AI answers earn only a small fraction of what they make from advertising, about one-tenth of 1% of ad revenues.

In response, Google not only offers its own AI chatbot, Gemini, but also incorporates AI features such as ' AI Summary ' and ' AI Mode ' into Google Search. It has been reported that Google is testing a program to pay media outlets that serve as sources of information when presenting information to users through these AI-related search features.

title: Google Wins Dismissal of PMC Lawsuit Over AI Search Snippets
description: The court said the issue isn't in the realm of antitrust laws and should be decided by lawmakers. Publishers have seen drops in search traffic because of AI overviews.
lead: Google has won dismissal of a lawsuit from Penske Media, parent of The Hollywood Reporter, Variety and Rolling Stone, accusing it of illegally using the publisher’s content to produce artificial intelligence-generated snippets of stories, which are displayed to users and undermines traffic to websites. U.S. District Judge Amit Mehta found on Wednesday that antitrust laws don’t account for AI overviews of content while nodding to “knock on consequences” to publishers whose “content Google takes and repurposes without compensation.” The issue, he concluded, is better-suited for lawmakers who must answer questions of economic dislocation caused by new technology.

title: Penske AI Overviews lawsuit dismissed because ‘no formal bargain’ struck with Google
description: A US judge has dismissed a lawsuit brought by Penske Media against Google over the loss of traffic and revenue as a result of AI Overviews.

Google is experimenting with paying publishers when their work contributes to AI-generated search answers, but early payouts vary dramatically. title: Variety owner Penske loses lawsuit against Google over lost search traffic
description: A judge ultimately determined that traffic was never promised as a trade-off for allowing AI robots to train on their content.
lead: A federal judge has tossed a lawsuit brought by Variety owner Penske and education tech venture Chegg over Google’s use of their content to train artificial intelligence-based products. Penske argued Google’s practices reduced referral traffic and revenue, but a judge ultimately determined that traffic was never promised as a trade-off for allowing AI robots to train on their content. The case was being closely watched by smaller, independent publishers to see if a legal precedent would be set, so they could seek redress from a court over Google’s predatory search and AI practices.

title: How AI summaries make it harder for NJ companies to reach consumers
description: With Google AI Overview, fewer users click on search links, a hurdle for NJ companies that relied on Google to drive traffic to their products.
lead: Google's AI Overviews summarize search results, causing some users to not click through to websites. Some New Jersey businesses are concerned about reduced website traffic, while others adapt by creating content that directly answers questions. Look up anything on Google and you’re presented with an artificial intelligence-generated summary above a list of relevant websites, known as Google AI Overview. But to the consternation of some New Jersey businesses, users often read only the AI summary, and don't bother clicking on the links to relevant websites.

title: Federal Court Just Dealt a Massive Blow to Publishers Suing Google AI
description: A federal judge dismissed antitrust lawsuits against Google's AI Overviews, ruling publishers have no legal right to search traffic.
lead: US District Judge Amit Mehta dismissed antitrust lawsuits from Chegg and Penske Media, ruling that Google’s AI Overviews do not violate antitrust laws simply by reducing search traffic to publisher websites. The court emphasized that traffic expectations are not legal contracts, leaving publishers to pursue commercial licensing deals or legislative relief instead. The ongoing battle between digital media and big tech over website traffic just hit a dramatic legal turning point. Online publishers hoping to use antitrust laws to stop Google’s AI Overviews from eating their traffic just suffered a major setback in court.

title: R27,700 Google Ads Spend Generates R309,700 in Sales
description: Press release: agency Bold Online publishes three South African Google Ads case studies, including a Performance Max campaign that generated R309,700 in sales from R27,700 of ad spend.
lead: Google Ads specialist agency Bold Online publishes three South African case studies focused on revenue, acquisition costs and return on ad spend. Johannesburg, 2 October 2026 - Bold Online Marketing (Pty) Ltd, a digital marketing and SEO agency based in Rosebank, Johannesburg, with an office in Cape Town, has published three Google Ads case studies demonstrating measurable commercial results for South African businesses. The results provide practical examples of how a ⁠Google Ads specialist agency ( can connect advertising spend to sales, revenue growth and customer acquisition costs.

title: Google pays media outlets for AI-generated content, but small websites risk losing traffic
description: Google has launched a pilot program under which about 100 publishers receive payment for the use of their content to generate AI-powered answers.
lead: Google has launched a pilot program in which about 100 publishers receive payment for the use of their content to generate AI-powered answers. At the same time, payments vary widely: some small media outlets have received less than $1,000 over several months, while larger participants can earn significantly more. For publishers, the problem isn’t just the amount of the payments. If a user receives a ready-made answer directly on Google, they may not visit the website where the information came from. This creates the risk of losing search traffic.

title: Google’s new content test could force publishers to prove they earned the click
description: Google updates guidelines to prioritize human effort, originality, and accuracy over AI-driven content and low-quality rewrites, transforming digital publishing
lead: Google’s guidance specifically flags summarising other people’s work without substantial value addition and combining content from multiple sources without adding value. Attribution alone, therefore, may not be enough to establish originality. The economics of publishing on the Internet have favored fast action. The quicker the publisher was able to spot a popular story, rephrase what had been written about it, and optimize it for the search engine, the higher were the chances of getting a lot of traffic from the search engine. However, the recently published Google guidelines suggest that things will be changing in the future.

title: 57% of beauty consumers don’t start with Google Search
description: Google, social, and AI aren’t replacing one another. They play different roles in the same journey, with big implications for search strategy.
lead: Consumers are moving across multiple platforms in a single purchase journey, with each one serving a different function. We asked respondents to walk us through their actual discovery process — not what they thought they should do, but what they actually did the last time they found a product they were curious about. The average respondent was 47 years old, with the largest cohorts in their 40s and 50s. This context makes the findings more interesting: These aren’t all Gen Z shoppers. They’re established, research-oriented consumers who are also using TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, and AI as part of their beauty purchase process.

title: ChatGPT and Gemini Gain Users as Google Holds Nearly 90% of Global Search Market
description: OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Google’s Gemini posted further gains in mobile usage in September, while Meta’s newly introduced Muse app approached... Read More
lead: OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Google’s Gemini posted further gains in mobile usage in September, while Meta’s newly introduced Muse app approached 2 million daily active users, according to Bank of America. The figures underscore growing demand for AI services even as Google retains a commanding share of traditional search. Bank of America analyst Justin Post, citing Sensor Tower estimates, said ChatGPT’s mobile daily active users increased 69% from a year earlier and 7% from August to a reported 664 million. Gemini’s audience expanded faster, rising 321% year over year and 11% month over month to a reported 151 million.

title: Google’s 1998 Incorporation: How It Changed Search Forever
description: Discover how a Stanford research project became Google, transformed search, built market dominance, and now faces a new competitive era shaped by AI.
lead: On September 4, 1998, Larry Page and Sergey Brin filed the paperwork to incorporate Google Inc. in California, turning a Stanford research project called BackRub into a registered company. The incorporation followed a $100,000 check from Sun Microsystems co-founder Andy Bechtolsheim, written out to “Google Inc.” before the company legally existed to cash it. Within days, Page and Brin moved their small operation into a rented garage in Menlo Park belonging to Susan Wojcicki, who later became the company’s 16th employee and eventually ran YouTube.

title: How bot traffic is wasting your ad budget and training Google to spend more
description: WebFX reports highlight how bot traffic wastes ad budgets by causing fake clicks and corrupting data, leading to inefficient targeting and wasted spend.
lead: Bot traffic is wasting your ad budget in two ways: The money it burns on fake clicks and fake leads, and the damage it does to the data your campaigns learn from. More than half of all web traffic is now automated, and a meaningful share of paid media spend can be exposed to traffic that will never buy. Understanding how bot traffic is wasting your ad budget starts with a shift in focus to what the problem actually is, WebFX reports. Bot traffic used to be a tracking problem, something you cleaned up in your analytics after the fact. In automated PPC (pay-per-click), it has become a bidding problem.

title: Google optimises its own revenue. Advertisers have to optimise theirs
description: Google's August 17 bidding change, AI Max defaults and court findings on ad pricing show a platform optimising its revenue while advertisers fight for theirs.
lead: That is the argument of this special edition, and it rests on a sentence that sounds obvious once it is said plainly. Google optimises for Google's revenue. Advertisers have to optimise for their own. Most of the time the two lines move together, which is why the auction works at all: a click that sells a product pays both sides. The trouble sits in the gaps where they part, and through 2026 those gaps have widened one default, one help-page edit and one removed control at a time. What follows draws on PPC Land's reporting and on coverage in Search Engine Roundtable, PPC News Feed, Digiday, AdExchanger, Adweek and MediaPost, going back to 2022 where the record requires it.

title: Microsoft, Meta And Google Just Silenced AI Spending Critics In One Earnings Night As Big Tech Capex Swells To $725B
description: Higher component costs, including memory chips, along with plans to build more data centers than previously anticipated, drove the upward revision in capex.

Google Cloud sales rose by a record 63%, sending the company’s shares over 6% higher in post-market hours. Alphabet, Inc. and Meta Platforms, Inc. on Wednesday raised their capital spending outlooks, with four of the biggest tech companies now projecting combined 2026 spending of up to $725 billion – bigger than the GDP of countries like Switzerland or Turkey.

title: Invalid traffic can wipe out unpaid Google ad revenue, MonetizeMore warns
description: Indonesian publishers heard Traffic Cop runs 100-plus checks per visitor but skips mobile apps. How far does a vendor's claimed access to Google's team go?
lead: MonetizeMore chief executive Kean Graham told publishers at a webinar organised with the Indonesian online media association AMSI that Google's invalid traffic enforcement can erase all unpaid ad revenue "overnight," and pitched the company's Traffic Cop detection tool, an AI assistant called Obi and an unreleased ad policy grader as the answer. The recording, titled "How Publishers Scale Ad Revenue & Prevent Policy Bans," was published on MonetizeMore's YouTube channel on October 8, 2026, the date used for this article.
